reviewed_semantics.authority_scope: Only explicitly declared PRIMARY/main/Russian primary clauses; GENERAL and named-objective branches retain original resolver behavior.
reviewed_semantics.selection: One recognized affirmed metric may resolve after directly negated aliases are excluded; direction/prediction/class-cardinality remain original MetricSpec.
reviewed_semantics.conflicts: Affirmed and negated same-name intersection is ambiguous; distinct affirmed names remain ambiguous; adjacent direct negators conservatively mark a conflict.
reviewed_semantics.negation_only: No affirmed recognized metric follows original unsupported/null path, never default RMSE/MacroF1.
reviewed_semantics.not_only_and_lists: Not-only/not-just constructions keep both mentions. A negator never expands to a following list; any subsequent unmatched metric remains affirmed and can preserve ambiguity.
reviewed_semantics.alias_overlap: Same containment rule as original _matches preserves composite aliases such as balanced accuracy and RMSE/RMSLE.
reviewed_semantics.budgets: Task text1MiB, primary clause250characters and max8bounded evidence entries unchanged; helper traverses only bounded primary clauses.
reviewed_semantics.failure_status_limit: A separate declaration containing only a negated metric can return unsupported before cross-declaration ambiguity; still null/failclosed, never a guessed objective.
reviewed_semantics.no_task_rewrite: Generic parser change only; original authority/task bytes were not read or rewritten in this review.

coverage: long aliases and repeated/multiline primary declarations
typed probability shape and bounded evidence

qualification_limits: Source-only review is not actual fixture PASS or universal natural-language negation understanding.
Only four direct primary-clause markers are supported; punctuation/intervening words or other negation forms conservatively retain old mentions.
Root integration, registered leased pure checks and fresh archive qualification remain required before actual Qwen/ML authority.
